videos.script: Most firewalls stand at the edge of the network, and trust everything inside. {{inside}} Then one server inside is taken over, and the edge has nothing to say about what it does next. {{lateral}} In this lesson the firewall moves onto the server itself. {{account}} It learns which account owns each connection, and stops the portal from reaching anything but its own front door. {{service}} It learns which service a socket belongs to. And you will catch one setting that looks right and does nothing at all. {{outbound}} Then the direction most people leave open: outbound. A server talks to very few places, so everything else is a signal. {{trace}} And when something is blocked, you follow one packet through the rules, and see which one decided.
